title: Composite shapes
summary: Find the area of a shape made from rectangles, triangles and parallelograms, by adding pieces or taking away a cut-out; trapezia as the stretch.

els.text: Area of shapes made from simpler shapes
Work out the area of a shape made from simpler shapes.

•  Split a shape into rectangles, triangles and parallelograms
•  Find a missing length before I calculate
•  Add the areas, or subtract a cut-out

els.text: A shape made by joining simpler shapes together.
The height measured at right angles to the base, not along a sloping side.
A quadrilateral with one pair of parallel sides.

slides.title: Discuss
slides.brief: Opens the lesson: the class finds that a rectangle and a triangle make the house.

els.text: This shape is not a rectangle, a triangle or a parallelogram. How could you find its area?
Split it into shapes we know. Find each area, then add them.

slides.title: Model M1
slides.brief: Models splitting a house shape: find the triangle's height from the wall and total heights, then each area, then add.

els.text: Work out the area of this shape.

slides.title: Set A A1
slides.brief: Rectangle and triangle. The wall and total heights are given, so the triangle's height is found first (7 − 4). Catches forgetting the half.

els.text: Find the area of this shape.

slides.title: Set A A2
slides.brief: A box with an identical triangle on each side. The sloping side (5) is marked as a distractor: the height is the width each triangle sticks out.

els.text: Work out the area of this shape. The two triangles are the same.
B and C: two triangles  $2 \times \tfrac12 \times 6 \times 4 = 24$ cm²

slides.title: Discuss
slides.brief: The sloping-side trap, named once for the whole lesson.

els.text: Sam says the area is $\tfrac12 \times 10 \times 13 = 65$ cm². What went wrong?
The height must be at right angles to the base. The sloping side is not the height.

slides.title: Set A A3
slides.brief: The triangle sits beside the rectangle, not on top: its base is the side of the rectangle, and its height is found from the widths (11 − 8).

els.text: Calculate the area of this shape.

slides.title: Set A C1
slides.brief: A parallelogram on a rectangle. The sloping side (5) is marked: catches using it as the height.

els.text: Work out the area of this shape.

slides.title: Model M2
slides.brief: Models whole minus cut-out for a shaded shape: the hole is a triangle.

slides.title: Set B B1
slides.brief: First subtract: a triangular hole in a rectangle, with one decimal length. Catches adding the two areas.

slides.title: Set B B2
slides.brief: A triangle inside a triangle: both areas use the triangle formula, then subtract. Catches adding, and halving only one of them.

slides.title: Model M4
slides.brief: Models a trapezium as a piece of a composite shape: find its height from the total, then use the trapezium formula (no splitting) and add the rectangle.

els.text: Find the area of this shape.

slides.title: Set D D1
slides.brief: A trapezium with a rectangular hole: the formula for the whole, then subtract. Catches not halving the sum of the parallel sides.

slides.title: Set D D2
slides.brief: A trapezium with a triangle on top: two formulas in one shape, and the triangle's height found from the total (9 − 5).

els.text: Work out the area of this shape.

slides.brief: Eight authored questions, printed four to an A4 page with a worked answer copy. Support fades: the split is drawn for 1 and 2, then it is independent; every house or side-triangle gives the total and the part, so the triangle's height is found by subtraction; 4 is a parallelogram with a triangle on top, 5 a rectangle cut out of a parallelogram, 6 a triangle frame (a triangle cut out of a triangle), 7 is a trapezium with a triangle on top, 8 a trapezium on a rectangle (the trapezium formula is used, never a split). Answers appear on a click.

slides.title: Exit ticket
slides.brief: Two shapes: one add, one subtract. The written part checks they can say why.

els.text: Find each area. Then write how you chose between adding and subtracting.

•  Split the shape into rectangles, triangles and parallelograms.
•  Find any missing length first.
•  Add the pieces, or take the hole away.
•  The height is always at right angles to the base.
